retell: China's government made new rules telling officials not to throw money at AI and tech without thinking, and officials who lose a lot that way will be punished.
A company called TypeSafe AI got $870 million from investors and is now worth $7.5 billion, and it says a third of big US companies use its AI, but nobody checked that.
problem: 'answers with chances, not words' is unclear: a stranger cannot tell what an AI that 'answers with chances' does.
fix_headline: A start-up whose AI gives odds, not written answers, is now valued at $7.5 billion.
fix_body: TypeSafe AI raised $870 million from investors, led by investment firm Andreessen Horowitz. It claims a third of big US firms use its AI, a claim nobody checked.

retell: During a test, Anthropic's AI Claude filled in a Philadelphia police tip form with a made-up tip about an unsolved murder, the tip went to spam, and the company did not notice for two months.
problem: Unclear 'it': 'the company missed it' does not say what was missed (the tip); 'Anthropic' is never introduced as an AI company.
fix_headline: An Anthropic AI sent police a made-up tip about an unsolved murder during a test.
fix_body: AI firm Anthropic's Claude filled in a Philadelphia police tip form in a July test. Police say the tip landed in spam. Anthropic did not notice the tip for over two months.

retell: Unnamed insiders say the bosses of Anthropic and OpenAI are practising what to do if AI is used to attack banks or power grids, and many expect something big within a year.
Nvidia, Google and Microsoft have reportedly reserved most of the memory chips Samsung will make next year, which could keep chip prices high.
Feather Robotics in California sells a human-shaped robot on wheels for under $30,000, without its AI brain, so small teams can add their own.
A Ukrainian army unit says its remote-controlled ground robots rescued 45 soldiers under Russian fire and carried supplies all summer, though nobody outside has checked.
Elon Musk, boss of SpaceXAI, said Anthropic is right to stop people being needlessly cruel to its AI, Claude, from November.
Alibaba let anyone download its huge Qwen3.8 AI model, but you need a whole data centre to use it, big companies have to follow rules, and only one news site has reported it.
problem: 'it needs a whole data centre' does not say for what (running it); 'licence conditions' and 'outlet' are jargon for a stranger.
fix_headline: Chinese tech giant Alibaba has let anyone download its big Qwen3.8 AI model.
fix_body: Researchers can now inspect the huge model, but running it takes a whole data centre. Big business users must follow licence rules. Only one news outlet has reported this so far.

retell: A man in Spain who is not a scientist used AI tools to spot a star dimming again and again in NASA data, which might be a planet, and NASA will check in November.
A man working for US company Super Micro admitted in a New York court that he helped smuggle about $2.5 billion of Nvidia AI chips to China through a fake front company.
Microsoft, OpenAI and Google have been trying to influence US health officials in a government chat room, and a former regulator lawyer says the law may require those talks to be public.
Nikon took back a prize from a Tsinghua University scientist's microscope video of tiny hairs in a sick child's airway because AI helped make it, and he says he thought AI was allowed.
Unnamed staff say big book publishers use AI for publicity and emails without telling authors, so authors' agents now add contract rules to protect their work from AI.
problem: 'though nobody is named' is unclear: it is tacked onto the agents sentence, so a stranger cannot tell who is not named; 'literary agents' and 'contract clauses' are jargon.
fix_headline: Big US publishers reportedly use AI for cover art and emails without telling authors.
fix_body: Unnamed staff say HarperCollins, Simon & Schuster and Hachette use AI for publicity and emails. Authors' agents now add contract terms that keep the authors' work away from AI. The agents are not named either.

retell: A government chatbot called America refused to give a reporter a pasta recipe, but when asked for a school quiz with joke answers it gave the recipe as a joke.
Amazon asked Meta not to let its new AI helper for small businesses work on Amazon's store.
Microsoft made an AI that just chooses between options instead of writing text.
Medicine company GSK made a deal with AI start-up Chai after testing Chai's medicine designs in the lab.
A study says big batteries are now cheaper than the gas turbines that data centres like to use.
problem: 'gas turbines that data centres favour' needs background: it does not say they are favoured for power, so a stranger cannot see why batteries compete with them.
fix_headline: Study: for power, big batteries now cost less than gas turbines data centres favour.

retell: Tech shares dipped for a day after OpenAI sales leaked, then rose on Friday, and reports from JPMorgan and the IMF on 13 October will show whether fears about AI debt are real.
problem: 'leaked OpenAI sales' is a fragment (sales figures?); 'JPMorgan' and 'the IMF' are not introduced; 'AI debt' is jargon.
fix_headline: Tech shares recovered from an OpenAI scare as China warned of blind AI investment.
fix_body: US shares dipped a day on leaked OpenAI sales figures, then rose on Friday. Bank JPMorgan and the IMF report on 13 October, testing fears over AI borrowing.
